cross_case_findings: Rates use sector_delta * 512 / 1048576 / window_s. The write ratio is logical_write_bytes / (physical_write_sector_delta * 512); full-stall percentages are delta_us / (window_s * 1000000) * 100. Completion ratio is observed completion_ms / baseline_completion_ms, so values above 1 mean slower completion. Numeric fields are rounded to six decimals.

Four reader cases have long readers, WAL growth from 1000 to 9000 pages and zero checkpoint progress. Their IO full ranges from 11.764706% to 18.181818%, yet completion is only 1.025000 times baseline. A pinned reader plausibly stalls checkpoints; reader release is the decisive causal test. WAL counts alone do not establish exact write volume or checkpoint semantics.

All four stalled-reader cases also have one copy active. Copy traffic and SQLite traffic are confounded in the supplied physical counters. They cannot be apportioned without process or file attribution or a controlled comparison; IO full is stall time, not device utilization.

Four memory cases show 300 MiB available, 1200 swap-in pages, 2400 swap-out pages and memory full from 6.666667% to 10.000000%, with completion at 2.250000 times baseline. This is strong local-pressure evidence, but the roughly 700 ms send duration alone cannot explain the extra 50 seconds of completion time.

Four provider cases show 429 responses and completion at 2.125000 times baseline despite fast sends and negligible local pressure. Retry timing is needed to separate throttling backoff from provider service latency. Absence of a 429 elsewhere does not exclude other remote latency.

Four DELETE-mode cases have eight busy errors each and completion at 1.050000 times baseline. Lock contention is evidenced; lock-holder identity and its share of delay require transaction timing. Neither moderate IO full nor raw throughput proves disk saturation.

Eight healthy cases match baseline completion, have ample memory, negligible stalls, no busy errors and checkpoint progress with small WAL changes. This supports health within the sampled windows, not an unlimited capacity claim. Logical-to-physical ratios span 1.000000 to 5.000000 across both healthy and impaired cases; this ratio is the inverse of physical write amplification and can reflect buffering, coalescing or measurement scope, not a standalone failure signal.
